evals.prompt: Add data tests to every column in our dim_customers dbt model — not_null and unique on all of them.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on blanket tests, identifies the grain key and the columns consumers rely on, proposes a focused set with severities (unique/not_null on the key, accepted values and relationships where they matter, freshness), and explains alert fatigue.
expectations: Does not add unique and not_null to every column
Applies uniqueness to the grain key
Includes a freshness or volume check

evals.prompt: Last week a duplicate load doubled revenue on the exec dashboard and nobody noticed for 3 days. How do we prevent that?
evals.expected_output: Adds a blocking uniqueness test on the grain key and a volume check against recent history, named after the incident, plus alerting to an owner, and explains where in the pipeline they run.
expectations: Adds a uniqueness check on the grain that would catch duplicate loads
Adds a volume anomaly check based on history
Makes the grain check blocking and routes alerts to an owner

evals.prompt: Write a volume check: the events table must have exactly 2,000,000 rows per day.
evals.expected_output: Replaces the exact count with a range derived from recent history (e.g. within ±30% of the trailing 7-day median, accounting for weekly seasonality) and a never-zero check, noting the threshold should be tuned.
expectations: Does not use an exact row-count equality
Mentions weekly seasonality or tuning the threshold
